CHOICE: 1
CONFIDENCE: 4

The large-scale limit is governed by the second Wiener chaos, not the first. The first chaos has spectral measure on the unit sphere, so it contributes nothing at low frequencies after rescaling. The second chaos has covariance proportional to K(r)², whose non-oscillatory part decays like r^{-(d-1)}. That kernel is the Riesz potential of (-Δ)^{-1/2}W, since (-Δ)^{-α}W has covariance |x|^{2α-d}, so 2α - d = -(d-1) gives α = 1/2. Solution 1 is correct. Solution 2 uses the decay of K itself rather than K², and Solution 3's spectral-density argument is not justified. I am fairly but not fully certain of the value, because I did not check it against the published result.
